Hi Lindsey — thanks again for the discussion today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Recap:
- Use case: semantic search over customer support docs and KB (mix of long articles and short FAQs). Primary goal is improved recall/precision for 0-3 sentence user queries and better reranking for related-article suggestions.
- Constraints: indexing size ~1.2M docs, initial pilot will run on a 25k-doc slice. Latency SLO for embed generation: <25ms per item at batch; cost sensitivity after pilot.
- Risks: embedding drift over time (content churn), dimensionality trade-offs for vector DB storage, and out-of-domain queries from enterprise customers.

What we’re sending (attached + links):
- prompt-set-searchly-v1.md (sample queries & prompt templates) - attached
- embeddings-benchmarks-searchly.csv (pilot benchmark samples + baseline metrics) - attached
- search-demo-recording.mp4 (screen share of live demo) - attached
- Benchmark & eval notebook: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/searchly-embeddings

Recommended short list to validate in pilot:
1) redwood-embed-large-v2 (1536 dims) - best initial fit for recall/MRR, higher cost
2) redwood-embed-compact-384 (384 dims, quantized) - cost-efficient candidate to test recall drop and storage savings
3) open-embed-lite (768 dims, open-source) - fallback for vendor neutrality testing

Evaluation plan (what we’ll measure):
- MAP@10, MRR, recall@100 on the pilot query set
- Diversity / nearest-neighbor stability (cosine distribution shift) to highlight drift
- Index size estimates and per-query latency at embedding + ANN lookup stage

Immediate asks for Searchly:
1) Share the 25k-document pilot slice (or give access to a GCS/ S3 path) - prefer JSONL with id, title, body
2) Seed ~200-500 labeled queries (we can use the provided prompt set to expand if needed)

Next steps:
- If you confirm dataset delivery, we’ll run the 3-model validation and share a short report (MAP/MRR tables + recommended next model) within 5 business days.
- Optional: 30-minute pre-eval call to align on labeling and metric thresholds - calendar link in the benchmark doc.

Thanks - looking forward.

--

Hi Lindsey - quick answers and recommendations:

1) HNSW (ef=128) - yes, we’ll run with your config to keep ANN behavior consistent for comparison. We’ll also run a small sensitivity sweep at ef=64/256 to show effect on recall/latency.

2) If you can only test one model initially: prioritize redwood-embed-large-v2. It preserves semantic granularity for mixed-length docs and should give the best MAP/MRR uplift; cost is higher but the pilot on 25k will let us quantify unit economics. If cost is a blocker, run redwood-embed-compact-384 first for an apples-to-apples cost comparison.

3) Drift detection recommendation: monthly sampling + cosine-similarity distribution monitoring on a fixed probe set (200 random doc vectors + 100 representative queries). Trigger alerts if the 75th percentile of probe-cosine drops by >0.08 or if nearest-neighbor entropy changes significantly. We can provide a small evaluation job that runs weekly and surfaces distribution diffs to your monitoring endpoint.

Deliverables we’ll produce after dataset drop:
- Pilot results spreadsheet (MAP/MRR/Recall@100 + per-model latency/cost estimates)
- Notebook with evaluation code and reproducible prompts: https://drive.redwood.ai/notes/searchly-embeddings-eval
- Short recommendation (go/no-go) and suggested reindex cadence

Proposed immediate schedule: once S3 location is available, I’ll schedule the 30-minute pre-eval tomorrow or the next day depending on your team’s availability.

--
Marcus
